applicability_predicate: Any scored assertion whose default threshold sits at or below the minimum of its own score range. The predicate is: with default configuration, no input can fail.
counterexample: An explicitly configured `threshold: 0` is a legitimate user choice and must still be honoured, which is why the fix used nullish coalescing rather than truthiness.
maps_to_existing_operator: none. Closest is the `vacuous` hole kind, which is a classification and not an operator.
not_applicable_cases: assertions whose threshold has no default and must be supplied
cases where an explicit 0 is deliberately configured, which remains valid

pair.defective_transformation: a wholly irrelevant conversation, default threshold
pair.expected_on_defective: FAIL. A default that cannot fail is not a check.

risks.false_negative: A default just ABOVE the floor, say 0.01, is nearly as vacuous and would not be caught by a test that only asks 'can anything fail'.
risks.false_positive: Treating a deliberate explicit 0 as the defect would report a hole in correct configuration.

semantic: An omitted threshold was treated as 0. The metric's score is a proportion in [0,1], so an entirely irrelevant conversation scoring 0 still passed. Fixed to default 0.5, with nullish coalescing so an explicit 0 stays valid.
title: conversation-relevance defaulted its threshold to 0, so everything passed
